Pope Leo begins respiratory therapy, recovery proceeding after lung surgery
Pope Leo XIV is recovering 'as expected' after undergoing lung cancer surgery in Rome on Oct. 13-14 according to Vatican officials and medical staff reports issued Wednesday following initial post-operative exams.
Pope Leo XIV underwent further medical exams and began respiratory physical therapy on Oct. 14, the day after undergoing lung cancer surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung.
In the first medical update from the Vatican since announcing Pope Leo's diagnosis, his doctors said that "recovery is proceeding as expected" and that he has started walking around his hospital room. Dr. Stefano Margaritora, the pope's surgeon, and Dr. Luigi Carbone, his personal doctor, said in a joint statement: "This morning, the Holy Father underwent the blood tests and chest X-ray scheduled following the surgery. The results confirm a normal postoperative recovery: the values are within the normal range for the type of surgery performed." They added, "The Holy Father underwent respiratory physical therapy and has begun walking around his room. He has resumed his regular diet, having had breakfast and lunch. His recovery is proceeding as expected."
Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said Pope Leo was "in good spirits" after surgery. Bruni also explained that prior to surgery on Oct. 13 at Gemelli Hospital in Rome, Pope Leo had undergone a robotic bronchoscopy with biopsy, a chest CT scan with contrast, and a PET scan which indicated surgical intervention was needed following an early-stage detection of a "well-contained" lung nodule.
According to Vatican News, additional post-operation tests will be conducted on tissue removed during surgery in coming days to determine if any cancer remains beyond what was excised.
Bruni said regarding timing for these test results: "You have to ask a doctor for the timing of those. It usually takes five, 10, 15 days depending on the situation." Medical experts speaking with OSV News indicated that analysis of lymph nodes could be important for determining next steps; Dr. Nirmal Veeramachaneni from St. Louis University School of Medicine said it would typically take about one week to receive all biopsy results.
The pope's doctors confirmed in their Oct. 14 statement that examination verified a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma as suspected by preoperative tests.
Adenocarcinoma is reported as being the most common form of lung cancer in the United States; it accounts for about 40% of all cases according to information from organizations such as Lung Cancer Foundation of America,according to Angelus News. The right lower lobe removed during Pope Leo’s operation constitutes roughly 30% of total lung capacity and is described as both the largest single lobe and located at the posterior-inferior part of the right chest cavity.
Pope Leo is expected to remain hospitalized at Gemelli Hospital for at least one week while recovering from surgery; all papal audiences have been canceled through Oct. 20 pending further updates about length-of-stay or upcoming travel plans including an anticipated trip Nov. 6-17 through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru—where Peru’s President Keiko Fujimori offered prayers for Pope Leo’s swift recovery.
